\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Circuit Layer Reduction}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.CircuitLayerReduction
\section{Overview}

This module proves the core iterative reduction theorem of the LMN argument: under a
composed Bernoulli random restriction, a function computed by a bounded-depth, bounded-fan-in
circuit has small decision-tree depth with high probability. The proof proceeds by strong
induction on the circuit depth $d$, with a base case ($d=2$) handled by the switching lemma
and an inductive step ($d\ge 3$) that factors the restriction parameter and applies a
two-stage argument to the children of the root gate.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Composed restriction parameter]
\lean{LMN.composedDelta}
\label{LMN.composedDelta}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b003}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b003
}
For a fan-in bound $w$, a width parameter $l$, and a depth $d$, the composed Bernoulli
restriction parameter is
\[
  \mathrm{composedDelta}(w,l,d) = \frac{1}{40w}\cdot\left(\frac{1}{40l}\right)^{d-2}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Positivity of the composed restriction parameter]
\lean{LMN.composedDelta_pos}
\label{LMN.composedDelta_pos}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composedDelta}
\difficulty{1}
Let $w$ be a positive integer fan-in bound, let $l > 0$ be a width parameter, and let
$d$ be any depth. Then the composed Bernoulli restriction parameter
\[
  \delta(w,l,d) = \frac{1}{40w}\cdot\left(\frac{1}{40l}\right)^{d-2}
\]
is strictly positive.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The composed restriction parameter is at most one]
\lean{LMN.composedDelta_le_one}
\label{LMN.composedDelta_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composedDelta}
\difficulty{2}
Let $w \ge 1$ be a natural number, let $l \ge 1$ be a real number, and let $d \ge 2$ be
a natural number. Then the composed Bernoulli restriction parameter satisfies
\[
  \frac{1}{40w}\cdot\left(\frac{1}{40l}\right)^{d-2} \le 1.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recursive step for the composed restriction parameter]
\lean{LMN.composedDelta_step}
\label{LMN.composedDelta_step}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composedDelta}
\difficulty{3}
Write $\delta(w,l,d) = \dfrac{1}{40w}\left(\dfrac{1}{40l}\right)^{d-2}$ for the composed
restriction parameter, with fan-in bound $w$, width parameter $l$, and depth $d$. For
natural numbers $w$ and $l$ and any depth $d \ge 3$,
\[
  \delta(w,l,d) = \frac{1}{40w}\,\delta(l,l,d-1).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recursive step for the composed restriction parameter]
\lean{LMN.composedDelta_step_right}
\label{LMN.composedDelta_step_right}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composedDelta}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a fan-in bound $w$, a width parameter $l > 0$, and a depth $d \ge 3$, and for these
values write $\delta(w,l,d)$ for the composed Bernoulli restriction parameter, namely
$\delta(w,l,d) = \frac{1}{40w}\left(\frac{1}{40l}\right)^{d-2}$. Then decreasing the
depth by one removes a single factor of $1/(40l)$:
\[
  \delta(w,l,d) = \delta(w,l,d-1)\cdot\frac{1}{40l}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Layer-2 data]
\lean{LMN.Layer2Data}
\label{LMN.Layer2Data}
\leanok
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002}
\uses{DNF, DNF.width}
A bundle describing the second layer of a circuit over $n$ variables: a number of gates,
a family of DNF formulas indexed by the gates, a common width bound $\mathrm{width}>0$ such
that every gate's width is at most $\mathrm{width}$, together with the hypothesis that within
each term of each gate distinct literals have distinct variables.
\end{definition}

\proofstep
  {LMN.Layer2Data}
  {context}
  {switching-lemma}
  {pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002}
\uses{DNF.eval, LMN.Layer2Data, LMN.switching_bernoulli_union_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{1}
Fix layer-2 data over $n \ge 1$ Boolean variables: a family of $N$ gates, each computing
a DNF formula, with a common width bound $w \ge 1$ so that every gate has width at most
$w$. Let $l \in \bbn$ and let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40 w}$ and $p
\le 1$. Consider a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, in
which each variable is independently left free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixed
to $0$ or to $1$, each with probability $\tfrac{1-p}{2}$. Then the probability that some
gate $i$ has restricted function $f_i\!\restriction_\rho$ (the gate's DNF evaluated on
the free coordinates, with the fixed coordinates set by $\rho$) of decision-tree depth
greater than $l$ satisfies
\[
\bbP\!\left[\,\exists\, i:\ \mathrm{depth}\big(f_i\!\restriction_\rho\big) > l\,\right]
  \;\le\; N\left(\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\big(-np/3\big)\right),
\]
where $\mathrm{depth}(g)$ denotes the least depth of a decision tree computing $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-step CNF replaceability for a layer of DNF gates]

  {LMN.Layer2Data}
  {context}
  {boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}
  {pdf-fc447f326910-p011-b004}
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF.eval, LMN.Layer2Data, LMN.one_step_reduction_failure_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{1}
Fix layer-2 data over $n \ge 1$ variables: a family of $m$ DNF gates $G_1, \dots, G_m$
together with a common width bound $w > 0$ satisfying $\mathrm{width}(G_i) \le w$ for
every $i$. Let $l \in \bbn$ and let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40\,w}$
and $p \le 1$. Then, under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$
variables, the probability that some gate fails the property — that is, the probability
that it is *not* the case that for every $i$ the restricted function $x \mapsto
G_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ agrees, on all inputs, with some CNF formula of width at
most $l$ — is at most
\[
  m\left(\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n p}{3}\right)\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Aggregating per-layer bounds into a total bound]
\lean{LMN.full_iterative_bound}
\label{LMN.full_iterative_bound}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.multi_stage_failure_bound}
\difficulty{1}
Fix a natural number $m$ and layer sizes $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_m \in \bbn$ whose total
satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^m \ell_i \le s$ for some $s \in \bbn$. Let $\alpha \ge 0$ and
$\beta$ be real numbers, and suppose $a_1, \dots, a_m$ are real quantities with $a_i \le
\ell_i\,\alpha$ for each $i$, together with a final real quantity $b$ satisfying $b \le
\beta$. Then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m a_i + b \;\le\; s\,\alpha + \beta.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Restricting by a composed restriction in two stages]
\lean{LMN.restrictFn_composeRestr'}
\label{LMN.restrictFn_composeRestr'}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composeRestr, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.extend, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be a Boolean function on
$n$ variables, and let $\rho_1, \rho_2$ be two restrictions on those variables, each
fixing some coordinates to Boolean values and leaving the rest free. Write $\rho_1 \circ
\rho_2$ for their composition, the restriction that on each coordinate uses the value
fixed by $\rho_1$ when there is one and otherwise the value assigned by $\rho_2$, and
for a restriction $\rho$ write $f\!\restriction_\rho$ for the function obtained from $f$
by fixing the coordinates set by $\rho$ and evaluating on the remaining free
coordinates. Then restricting $f$ by the composition $\rho_1 \circ \rho_2$ gives the
same function as first restricting $f$ by $\rho_1$ and then restricting the function
$f\!\restriction_{\rho_1}$ by $\rho_2$:
\[
f\!\restriction_{\rho_1 \circ \rho_2} \;=\;
\bigl(f\!\restriction_{\rho_1}\bigr)\!\restriction_{\rho_2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Two-stage bound for composed Bernoulli restrictions]
\lean{LMN.two_stage_bound'}
\label{LMN.two_stage_bound'}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composeRestr, LMN.restriction_compose_eq, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb_le_one', SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight_nonneg', SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight_sum_one}
\difficulty{5}
Let $p_1, p_2 \in (0,1]$, let $E$ and $A$ be predicates on restrictions of $n$
variables, and let $\beta \ge 0$. For a parameter $p$ write $\bbP_p[\,\cdot\,]$ for the
Bernoulli event probability under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction, and for two
restrictions $\rho_1, \rho_2$ write $\rho_1 \ast \rho_2$ for their composition (using
the value $\rho_1$ fixes on each coordinate, and otherwise the value from $\rho_2$).
Suppose that for every restriction $\rho_1$ with $\neg A(\rho_1)$ one has
$\bbP_{p_2}\!\left[\, E(\rho_1 \ast \rho_2) \,\right] \le \beta$. Then
\[
  \bbP_{p_1 p_2}[E] \;\le\; \bbP_{p_1}[A] + \beta .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of the depth-threshold probability]
\lean{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_dtDepth_mono}
\label{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_dtDepth_mono}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_mono, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{1}
Fix a parameter $p$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, a Boolean function $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to
\mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$, and thresholds $l_1 \le l_2$. Under a Bernoulli($p$)
random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, the probability that the restricted
function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater
than $l_2$ is at most the probability that it has decision-tree depth strictly greater
than $l_1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Congruence of the depth-exceedance probability for equal functions]
\lean{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_congr_fn'}
\label{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_congr_fn'}
\leanok
\uses{SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{1}
Fix a real parameter $p$, a threshold $t \in \bbn$, and two Boolean functions $f, g :
(\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$ that agree at every input, so
$f(x) = g(x)$ for all $x$. Draw a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ of the $n$
variables, write $h_\rho$ for the restricted function obtained from a Boolean function
$h$ under $\rho$, and let $D(\cdot)$ denote decision-tree depth. Then
\[
  \bbP_p\!\left[\,D(f_\rho) > t\,\right] = \bbP_p\!\left[\,D(g_\rho) > t\,\right],
\]
i.e.\ the two functions assign the same probability to the event that the restricted
function has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Switching bound for depth-2 circuits]
\lean{LMN.depth2_circuit_switching_bound}
\label{LMN.depth2_circuit_switching_bound}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p008-b005}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p001-b008,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p002-b001,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p002-b002,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p002-b003,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p002-b004
}
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Circuit.maxFanin, BoolCircuit.Circuit.size, BoolCircuit.Lit.eval, BoolCircuit.Lit.toLiteral, CNF.eval, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_congr_fn', LMN.depth2AndToCNF, LMN.depth2AndToCNF_eval, LMN.depth2AndToCNF_width_le, LMN.depth2OrToDNF, LMN.depth2OrToDNF_eval, LMN.depth2OrToDNF_width_le, LMN.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_cnf_general, LMN.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_dnf_general, Literal.eval, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, Term.eval, Term.width, dtDepth}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n\ge 1$ variables that is
computed by some Boolean circuit of depth at most $2$, size at most $s$, and fan-in at
most $w$, where $w\ge 1$. Fix a real parameter $p$ with $0<p\le \tfrac{1}{40w}$ (so in
particular $p\le 1$), and draw a random restriction $\rho$ in which each of the $n$
variables is, independently, left free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixed to the
value $0$ or to the value $1$, each with probability $\tfrac{1-p}{2}$. Write $f_\rho$
for the restriction of $f$ by $\rho$ (the function $x\mapsto f$ evaluated at the
assignment agreeing with $\rho$ on its fixed coordinates and with $x$ on the free ones),
and let $D(g)$ denote the least depth of a decision tree computing a function $g$. Then
for every $t\in\bbn$,
\[
\Pr_{\rho}\!\left[\, D(f_\rho) > t \,\right]\ \le\ \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} +
\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right).
\]
\end{lemma}

  {direct}

  {pdf-fc447f326910-p008-b005,
    pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004}
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Circuit.maxFanin, BoolCircuit.Circuit.size, DecisionTree.eval, LMN.composedDelta, LMN.composedDelta_le_one, LMN.depth2_circuit_switching_bound, LMN.dtDepth_restrictFn_le', SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight_sum_one, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n\ge 1$ variables, let
$s,w,l\ge 1$ be positive integers, let $t\ge 0$, and suppose $f$ is computed by a
Boolean circuit of depth at most $2$, size at most $s$, and fan-in at most $w$. Draw a
random restriction $\rho$ that leaves each variable free independently with probability
$p=\tfrac{1}{40w}$ and otherwise fixes it to $0$ or $1$, each with probability
$\tfrac{1-p}{2}$. Writing $D(g)$ for the least depth of a decision tree computing a
Boolean function $g$, and $f\!\restriction_\rho$ for the function obtained from $f$ by
substituting the fixed values of $\rho$ and keeping the free coordinates as inputs, the
probability that the restricted function is hard to compute by a shallow decision tree
satisfies
\[
  \Pr_{\rho}\!\big[\,D(f\!\restriction_\rho) > t\,\big]
  \le (s-1)\left(\tfrac12\right)^{l} + \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t}
+ (s-1)\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120w}\right) + s\,\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120l}\right).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Union bound for a random restriction over a list of circuits]
\lean{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_list_union_bound}
\label{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_list_union_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_union_bound_fin, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb}
\difficulty{4}
Fix a parameter $p$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, and consider a Bernoulli$(p)$ random
restriction on $n$ variables, under which each variable is independently left free with
probability $p$ and fixed to each of the two Boolean values with probability $(1-p)/2$.
Let $c_1, \dots, c_m$ be a list of Boolean circuits on $n$ variables, and for each
circuit $c$ let $\mathrm{bad}(c, \cdot)$ be a predicate on restrictions. Then the
probability that some circuit in the list is bad is at most the sum of the individual
probabilities:
\[
\Pr_p\!\left[\exists\, i,\ \mathrm{bad}(c_i, \rho)\right] \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^{m}
\Pr_p\!\left[\mathrm{bad}(c_i, \rho)\right],
\]
where each term is the probability, under the same random restriction, that the
corresponding predicate holds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Inductive step of the circuit-to-decision-tree reduction]
\lean{LMN.circuit_reduction_ind_step}
\label{LMN.circuit_reduction_ind_step}
\leanok
\proofsource{switching-lemma}{
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b003
}
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b003,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p013-b002
}
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Circuit.maxFanin, BoolCircuit.Circuit.size, DecisionTree.depth, DecisionTree.eval, LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_list_union_bound, LMN.child_size_le_parent, LMN.children_depth_le, LMN.children_maxFanin_le, LMN.children_size_sum_le, LMN.composedDelta, LMN.composedDelta_le_one, LMN.composedDelta_pos, LMN.composedDelta_step_right, LMN.compress_and_switch, LMN.dtDepth_restrictFn_le', LMN.two_stage_bound', SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb_le_one', SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{7}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n \ge 1$ variables, and fix
natural numbers $d,s,w,l,t$ with $d \ge 3$ and $s,w,l \ge 1$. Suppose $f$ is computed by
a Boolean circuit of depth at most $d$, size at most $s$, and maximum fan-in at most
$w$. For parameters $w,l$ and a depth $e$, write $\delta_e =
\frac{1}{40w}\left(\frac{1}{40l}\right)^{e-2}$ for the composed restriction parameter;
let $D(g)$ denote the decision-tree depth of a Boolean function $g$, and let $g|_\rho$
denote its restriction by a restriction $\rho$. Assume the following inductive
hypothesis: for every Boolean function $g$ on $n$ variables and every integer $s' \ge
1$, if $g$ is computed by a circuit of depth at most $d-1$, size at most $s'$, and
maximum fan-in at most $w$, then under a Bernoulli random restriction $\rho$ with
parameter $\delta_{d-1}$,
\[
\Pr_{\rho}\!\left[D(g|_\rho) > l\right] \le (s'-1)(1/2)^{l} + (1/2)^{l} +
(s'-1)\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120w}\right) + s'\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120l}\right).
\]
Then under a Bernoulli random restriction $\rho$ with parameter $\delta_{d}$,
\[
\Pr_{\rho}\!\left[D(f|_\rho) > t\right] \le (s-1)(1/2)^{l} + (1/2)^{t} +
(s-1)\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120w}\right) + s\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120l}\right).
\]
\end{lemma}

\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Circuit.maxFanin, BoolCircuit.Circuit.size, LMN.circuit_reduction_ind_base, LMN.circuit_reduction_ind_step, LMN.composedDelta, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n\ge 1$ variables, and let
$d\ge 2$, $s\ge 1$, $w\ge 1$, and $l\ge 1$ be positive integers together with an integer
threshold $t\ge 0$. Suppose $f$ is computed by some Boolean circuit of depth at most
$d$, size at most $s$ (counting gates and literal leaves), and fan-in at most $w$. Let
$\rho$ be a Bernoulli random restriction on the $n$ variables with survival parameter
\[
  p = \frac{1}{40w}\left(\frac{1}{40l}\right)^{d-2},
\]
so that each variable is independently left free with probability $p$ and otherwise
fixed to $0$ or to $1$, each with probability $(1-p)/2$. Write $f\restriction_\rho$ for
the function obtained from $f$ by substituting the values $\rho$ assigns and keeping the
free coordinates as inputs, and let $D(g)$ denote the least depth of a decision tree
computing a Boolean function $g$. Then
\[
  \bbP\!\left[D(f\restriction_\rho) > t\right]
  \;\le\; (s-1)\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{t}
    + (s-1)\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120\,w}\right)
    + s\,\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120\,l}\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Random-restriction bound on the decision-tree depth of a small circuit]

\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Circuit.maxFanin, BoolCircuit.Circuit.size, LMN.circuit_reduction_ind, LMN.composedDelta, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n \ge 1$ variables, and let
$d,s,w,l,t \in \bbn$ satisfy $d \ge 2$ and $s,w,l \ge 1$. Suppose $f$ is computed by
some Boolean circuit of depth at most $d$, size at most $s$, and maximum fan-in at most
$w$. Write $f\!\restriction_\rho$ for the restriction of $f$ by a restriction $\rho$,
and let $D(g)$ denote the decision-tree depth of a Boolean function $g$, that is, the
least depth of a decision tree computing it. Then, under a Bernoulli random restriction
$\rho$ with parameter $\delta = \dfrac{1}{40w}\left(\dfrac{1}{40l}\right)^{d-2}$,
\[
  \bbP\bigl[\, D(f\!\restriction_\rho) > t \,\bigr]
  \;\le\; s\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{t}
    + s\,\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120w}\right) + s\,\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120l}\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Switching-lemma bound on decision-tree depth after a random restriction]
\lean{LMN.circuit_reduction_core}
\label{LMN.circuit_reduction_core}

\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Circuit.maxFanin, BoolCircuit.Circuit.size, LMN.circuit_reduction_aux, LMN.composedDelta, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n\ge 1$ variables, and let
$d,s,w,l,t$ be natural numbers with $d\ge 2$ and $s,w,l\ge 1$. Suppose $f$ is computed
by some Boolean circuit of depth at most $d$, size at most $s$, and fan-in at most $w$.
Draw a random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables in which each variable is
independently left free with probability
\[
  p \;=\; \frac{1}{40w}\left(\frac{1}{40l}\right)^{d-2},
\]
and is otherwise fixed to $0$ or to $1$, each with probability $(1-p)/2$; let
$f\restriction_\rho$ denote the function of the free variables obtained by substituting
the fixed values into $f$. Then the probability that $f\restriction_\rho$ cannot be
computed by any decision tree of depth at most $t$ satisfies
\[
  \bbP\!\left[\,\text{decision-tree depth of } f\restriction_\rho > t\,\right]
  \;\le\; s\left(\tfrac12\right)^{l} + \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t}
  + s\,\exp\!\left(-\frac{n}{120w}\right) + s\,\exp\!\left(-\frac{n}{120l}\right).
\]
\end{theorem}
